items.basis: The claimed improvement in droplet separation without increased flow resistance violates fundamental fluid dynamics principles; higher separation efficiency typically requires increased surface area or longer residence time, both of which increase pressure drop

The 8 bar pressure boundary is insufficiently addressed for erosion concerns; at this pressure, any particulate matter in the air stream will accelerate dramatically through the vanes, causing rapid erosion that would degrade performance far below the claimed 500-hour service interval
The candidate provides no empirical evidence to support the 35 mbar pressure drop claim or the 30% reduction in wall deposits, making these predictions entirely unsubstantiated assertions

The testable prediction only claims to match the baseline separator's performance (12°C dew point) rather than improve it, offering no solution to the core problem of liquid water carryover during high-demand cycling

The helical vane pack with 22 stages cannot be practically manufactured at 1/2 inch diameter with the claimed 15-45 degree helix angle variation; the mechanical tolerances required would make production impossible with standard manufacturing techniques

The dew point measurement within 0.5 C is insufficiently precise to detect meaningful improvements in separation performance, especially during transient cycling conditions where the actual failure occurs
